claim: Let \(\mathcal F_{14}=(\omega^{mn})_{m,n\in\mathbb Z_{14}}\), where \(\omega=e^{-2\pi i/14}\), and let \(\mathcal F_{14}[\mathcal M,:]\) be the rows indexed by a nonempty proper subset \(\mathcal M\subset\mathbb Z_{14}\). This row-selected harmonic frame is full spark if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is uniformly distributed over the divisors of \(14\) and, up to an affine map \(x\mapsto ax+b\) with \(a\in\mathbb Z_{14}^{\times}\), neither \(\mathcal M\) nor its complement is one of \(\{0,1,3,4\}\), \(\{0,1,2,3,6\}\), \(\{0,1,2,3,6,11\}\), or \(\{0,1,2,3,5,6,11\}\). The seven exceptional affine orbits occur in cardinalities \(4,5,6,7,8,9,10\), with the cardinality-seven orbit self-complementary. Equivalently, exactly \(1834\) nonempty proper row sets are full spark; among the \(2142\) uniformly distributed row sets, exactly \(308\) fail full spark.
integrity: The proof combines published general necessity with affine/complement invariance, exhaustive residue-class orbit enumeration, exact cyclotomic zero witnesses, and reproducible two-prime finite-field certificates with no floating-point acceptance decisions.
scientific_limitations: Exact finite classification at Fourier order 14 only; no general composite-order characterization is claimed. Literature search cannot exclude differently phrased or unindexed prior statements.
title: Complete full-spark classification for row subsets of the order-\(14\) Fourier matrix
